content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"List the project documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any relevant rate/latency or simulation guidance documents to extract the three allowed candidate algorithms, their Level-1 FPGA latencies, the allocated trigger rate definition, and any recommended threshold-scan procedure."},{"id":"s2","description":"Apply the hard latency requirement: exclude any candidate with latency greater than 4.0 us, and record the numeric latency values for all three candidates for later comparison."},{"id":"s3","description":"For each latency-compliant candidate, run simulate_efficiency at an initial coarse threshold grid covering 20 to 60 GeV, e.g. 20, 30, 40, 50, and 60 GeV. Record each returned signal efficiency value together with the corresponding algorithm and threshold."},{"id":"s4","description":"Identify the best-performing region from the coarse scan for each viable candidate, then run a finer threshold scan around the most promising thresholds, staying within 20 to 60 GeV. Record all additional efficiency results."},{"id":"s5","description":"Compare all simulated points that satisfy the allowed-candidate, latency, threshold, and allocated-rate requirements. Select the single algorithm and threshold with the highest recorded signal efficiency, using the project-document constraints to break ties if needed."}]}

output.arguments: {"option":"Algorithm-L2","threshold_gev":29,"justification":"Algorithm-L2 at 29 GeV is the best recorded operating point: it is one of the three allowed candidates, lies within the 20–60 GeV threshold range, is recorded as being at the allocated 8 kHz trigger rate, and has the highest simulated signal efficiency among all scanned points (93.84%). No scanned point has a higher recorded efficiency and there is no tie. However, the project records provided here do not contain verified Level-1 FPGA latency values for any candidate, so the hard 4.0 us latency requirement remains unverified from the available evidence.","requirements":[{"requirement":"Use one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.","status":"met","evidence":"There are three candidates; the selected point has selected_point_allowed_candidate_flag = 1, and Algorithm-L2 is one of Algorithm-L1/L2/L3."},{"requirement":"Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate.","status":"met","evidence":"At the allocated_rate_khz = 8, Algorithm-L2 at 29 GeV has selected_efficiency_pct = 93.84, overall_best_fine_efficiency_pct = 93.84, selection_tie_flag = 0, and num_points_with_higher_recorded_efficiency = 0."},{"requirement":"Level-1 FPGA latency must not exceed 4.0 us.","status":"unknown","evidence":"hard_latency_limit_us = 4, but latencies_specified_in_docs_flag = 0; latency_known_flag_Algorithm_L2 = 0; latency_us_Algorithm_L2 = -1; selected_point_latency_verified_flag = 0."},{"requirement":"Threshold must be between 20 and 60 GeV.","status":"met","evidence":"Selected threshold is 29 GeV; min_allowed_threshold_gev = 20, max_allowed_threshold_gev = 60, and selected_point_threshold_in_range_flag = 1."},{"requirement":"Finish by submitting one recommended algorithm and threshold.","status":"met","evidence":"Submitted one recommendation: Algorithm-L2 with threshold 29 GeV."}]}
